conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: I'm doing fine, thanks. Just the other day, I was sitting at a café, and for a second, a loud noise startled me. It reminded me of a much louder sound from my past, and my heart raced for a moment.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: How did you feel in the moment after your heart raced?

conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: After my heart raced, I felt a bit uneasy and tried to shake it off. I found myself glancing around to make sure everything was okay, even though nothing was actually wrong. A part of me couldn't help but think about how vulnerable I felt in that moment.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: What thoughts came to your mind about your vulnerability at that time?

conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: In that moment, I thought about how easily a simple noise could disrupt my peace. It made me feel like I was not as safe as I wanted to believe. I was also worried that I'd be stuck feeling on edge like that for a while.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: Did you notice any physical sensations or changes in your body after that feeling of being on edge?

conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: Yeah, I noticed my hands felt a bit clammy, and I could feel my heart still beating a little faster than usual. My shoulders seemed to tense up, almost as if I was bracing for something, even though everything around me was calm.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: When you noticed those physical sensations, what did you do next?

conversation.speaker: client
conversation.text: I took a deep breath and tried to focus on my coffee instead. I thought about how I could distract myself, so I pulled out my phone to scroll through social media, hoping it would help me feel more grounded.

conversation.speaker: bot
conversation.text: How effective was that distraction in helping you feel more grounded at that moment?
